newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.

text.p: The shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar and currency basket on Wednesday in very dull trading during the Jewish Passover holiday, dealers said.

"Trading was extremely quiet today as many investors went on vacation. The shekel weakened slightly against the dollar after it rose sharply on Thursday amid fears that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu whould be charged with fraud and breach of trust," a dealer at Bank Hapoalim said.

After the setting of the representative rate on Thursday prosecutors slapped down police recommendations that Netanyahu be charged in a corruption scandal. Prosecutors found insufficient evidence to issue the first indictment against an Israeli prime minister.
"Now the political situation seems to be stable again and the shekel continued to recover today," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3990 shekels against 3.4020 on Friday the last day the representative rate was fixed before the holiday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6787 shekels against 3.6809 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6962 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7014 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9828 shekels after 1.9821 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3980 shekels.
